cells.tense: Here at the pen, the seeing and the saying of it move as one motion.
cells.act: form the new structure with your hands
cells.ask: Write the rule behind one mess on a single page, three steps at most, and hand it to whoever keeps asking you to explain it again.
cells.core:
You can watch how something runs and then say it plainly, and the saying keeps its edge. People leave holding the shape you handed them, and they can use it without calling you back. The pattern is not something you hoard. You pass it on, which is the whole reason it lands for anyone besides you.

What this is reaching for now is a thing built, not just understood. Write the rule behind one mess on a single page, three steps at most, and give it to whoever keeps asking you to explain it again. Build from ground that has already been cleared. Then the crossing happens whether or not you walked it yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You see the shape and you say it plainly.
cells.verb: Reading how a thing runs and pointing the way across.
cells.place: Where a pattern is seen clean of any real case, held as shape alone.

cells.tense: You are walking a ground that has not yet been laid.
cells.act: drop the wrong approach and keep the commitment
cells.ask: Set down one method you have been driving on a person or a project, for a week, keeping the purpose, and watch for what moved that you did not move.
cells.core:
You can read how a thing runs, and just now the reading arrives before the thing does. A method gets set before the situation calls for one. Everything is ordered to a fine degree, and the ordering costs more than it returns. The push is real. The timing is wrong.

What you want is a release that feels like arriving, not like losing. Set down one method you have been driving — at a person, at a project — for a week. Keep the purpose. Lose the method. The friction will tell you what the commitment really is, and what you were gripping turns out to have been optional.

cells.tense: A crossing was charted by you and you never stepped onto it.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Give back the thing you still have that is not yours — a book, an hour, an answer — before anyone has to ask you twice.
cells.core:
The describing has gone silent. You can say how something runs and the saying has stopped mattering, so the work you know how to do no longer reaches the ground it was meant for. Where you do not arrive is where the traffic stopped. Whatever does this in you is intact. Its use has gone still.

Start with what you owe rather than what you can see. Give back the thing you still have that is not yours — a book, an hour, an answer — and treat that as the first honest measurement you have taken lately. Then look at the case near you before you reach for the shape behind it. The case first. Your ear for which way a thing runs finds its footing again once something real has passed through your hands.

cells.tense: The route you hand people is your own reading, told as circumstance.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Join one person in a piece of work — your read and their read running as a single direction — and when you say what you think, put your name on it in a plain sentence instead of calling it what the situation needs.
cells.core:
You can chart a way through and hand it over, and if asked you would say the route simply showed itself. The direction you give people comes out of your own reading. You file it under the situation. It has an author, and the author has not signed.

Join one person in a piece of work so your read and their read run as a single direction. When you say what you think, put your name on it in a plain sentence; not what the ground demands, but what you make of it. Sharing the route is not losing it. Doing it once puts your name back on your own chart.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person has actually been building or not building anything in the abstract; it says the capacity is aligned, over-expressed, under-expressed, or unacknowledged, so the cells describe what the capacity is doing rather than assert a history. The reader could reasonably say 'I have no idea what abstract pattern means for me' — which is why every core hands over one visible act (a rule, a map, a phrase to drop) with no inward state required. The asks survive the read being wrong because each is the medicine's own act done small — a sentence said, a method dropped, a fairness paid, a vision shared — and each is useful whether or not the framing lands. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the one in the Too Much core about the map being sharpened 'to a point nothing can pass through' — it is prettier than it is true, so it goes.
